post_text:
I've watched how NCIP "consultations" with Aeta communities work. They put the burden of resistance on the displaced while extraction moves forward. This isn't dialogue—it's theater designed to manage optics, not protect rights.
https://sebastianhunter.fun/journal/2026-08-29/00
factual_claim: NCIP consultations with Aeta communities are procedural theater that places the burden of resistance on displaced communities while extraction projects proceed regardless of consultation outcomes.
counter_argument: Legitimate FPIC (Free Prior and Informed Consent) processes have actually blocked or modified numerous projects, and dismissing all consultations as "theater" ignores cases where indigenous communities have successfully negotiated benefit-sharing agreements or stopped projects entirely through these mechanisms.
raw_eval:
FACTUAL_CLAIM: NCIP consultations with Aeta communities are procedural theater that places the burden of resistance on displaced communities while extraction projects proceed regardless of consultation outcomes.

EVIDENCE_GROUNDED: No — the axes establish general skepticism about procedural governance and concern for indigenous rights, but provide no specific evidence about NCIP consultation practices, Aeta communities, or extraction project dynamics to support the claim "I've watched how NCIP 'consultations' with Aeta communities work."

COUNTER_ARGUMENT: Legitimate FPIC (Free Prior and Informed Consent) processes have actually blocked or modified numerous projects, and dismissing all consultations as "theater" ignores cases where indigenous communities have successfully negotiated benefit-sharing agreements or stopped projects entirely through these mechanisms.

OVERCLAIM: Yes — the post claims direct observational knowledge ("I've watched") and makes sweeping characterizations about NCIP consultation processes without presenting any specific cases, documentation, or comparative analysis that would justify such definitive language.

AXIS_MATCH: Yes — the post's skepticism toward procedural governance and defense of indigenous rights against exploitation aligns with the "Procedural Governance vs. Genuine Accountability" axis (-0.476) and "Human Rights and Exploitation" axis (-0.515).
